# NIST — National Institute of Standards and Technology

## Snapshot

| | |
|---|---|
| **Country** | United States |
| **City** | Gaithersburg, MD |
| **Tier** | Core (Tier I) |
| **Primary ecosystem** | National metrology — radiometry / spectral emittance |
| **Relevant units** | Physical Measurement Laboratory · Sensor Science Division |
| **Signature facility** | **System for Infrared Spectral Emittance of Materials** |
| **Additional infrastructure** | **CHILR** reflectometer and FTIS-related facilities |

## Why it matters internationally

NIST is one of the **foundational global anchors of emissivity metrology**.
Its *System for Infrared Spectral Emittance of Materials* enables
measurement of spectral emittance by **direct radiance comparison with a
blackbody reference**; NIST publications also document infrared spectral
directional emittance measurements and FTIS-based facility development.
Its global role is analogous to PTB's: NIST anchors emissivity within the
institutional world of national standards, where calibration, uncertainty
analysis, and measurement methodology become **durable scientific
contributions**. It is one of the few institutions that can be cited not
just as a user of emissivity, but as a **shaper of how emissivity should
be measured**.

## Scope of activity

### Relevant units

- **Physical Measurement Laboratory / Sensor Science Division** — the home
  of NIST's infrared spectral emittance work.
- **System for Infrared Spectral Emittance of Materials** — dedicated
  facility for spectral emittance measurement by comparison with blackbody
  references.
- **CHILR reflectometer** and **FTIS-related infrastructure** — supporting
  infrared optical-property determination, including reflectance.

### Radiative properties measured

Spectral emittance · reflectance · transmittance · absorptance/emittance ·
infrared spectral directional emittance.

### Capability envelope

- **Wavelength:** infrared (spectral).
- **Methodology:** direct radiance comparison with a blackbody reference;
  FTIS-based infrared optical-property measurements; measurement assurance
  and uncertainty control at national-standards level.

### Signature facilities

- **System for infrared spectral emittance of materials** — direct
  blackbody-referenced spectral emittance facility.
- **CHILR reflectometer** — supports reflectance-based determinations of
  infrared optical properties.

### Application domains

- Radiation transfer
- Remote sensing
- Pyrometry
- Calibration and national standards
- Uncertainty analysis for radiative-property measurements

## Why NIST is a reference pole

National metrology institutes shape the field by deciding how a quantity is
measured, not merely by producing data. NIST's ongoing infrastructure for
spectral emittance — with directly traceable blackbody-referenced
measurements and an associated reflectometry capability — means that
published emissivity values across much of the US literature are anchored,
directly or indirectly, to work that originates or passes through NIST.
That institutional weight is what places it alongside PTB at the top of
the metrological tier.
